name: CreateEndpointConfiguration
description:
Create endpoint configurations.

Endpoint Configurations allow you to configure specific endpoints taht can be used for example for EventExportConfigurations.

- Make sure to catch & store the `SecretKey1` and `SecretKey2`, as there will be no other way of retrieving them after this service call!
auth_description: Requires a user of type `Employee` or `Api` with functionality `EndpointConfigurations:Create`

headers.name: EVA-User-Agent
headers.description: The user agent that is making these calls. Don't make this specific per device/browser but per application. This should be of the form: `MyFirstUserAgent/1.0.0`

headers.name: EVA-Requested-OrganizationUnitID
headers.description: The ID of the organization unit to run this request in.

headers.name: EVA-Requested-OrganizationUnit-Query
headers.description: The query that selects the organization unit to run this request in.

request_samples.name: CURL

D.name: Certificate
D.description:
A client certificate that can be used for mTLS. Must be X509 in PKCS12 format. Also, it must not be expired, have a private key and have clientAuth in it's extended key usage.

While this property is not required, if it is sent in the request it must have a valid value.

D.name: Password
D.description:
The password that is used to encrypt the certificate.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

E.name: Passphrase
E.description:
The passphrase that is used to encrypt the private key.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

E.name: PrivateKey
E.description:
The SSH private key, as PEM or OpenSSH text. It must be readable with the given `Passphrase`.

While this property is not required, if it is sent in the request it must have a valid value.

C.name: BasicPassword
C.description:
This will yield a basic authorization header with this password - combine with `BasicUsername`.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: BasicUsername
C.description:
This will yield a basic authorization header with this username - combine with `BasicPassword`.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: ClientCertificate
C.description:
Configuration for Mutual TLS (mTLS)

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: Headers
C.description:
Additional headers sent with every request to this endpoint. Header names starting with `X-EVA-`, `Content-*` headers, and `Authorization` (when another authorization scheme is configured) are reserved and will be rejected.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: SshKey
C.description:
The SSH private key for an `Sftp` endpoint, as an alternative or addition to `BasicPassword`. Only supported on `Sftp` endpoints.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: StaticBearerToken
C.description:
This will result in an authorization header that looks like: `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

C.name: StaticUnschemedToken
C.description:
This will result in an authorization header that looks like: `Authorization: TOKEN`. Use this only when the other options are not sufficient.

Providing a `null` value and not providing the property at all has different meanings.

F.name: Comment
F.description:
A free-text comment, for example how the fingerprint was verified. When an already pinned host key is supplied again without a comment, its comment is kept.

This string must be between 0 (incl) and 500 (incl) characters long.

F.name: Fingerprint
F.description: The SHA256 fingerprint of the host key, as shown by `ssh-keygen -lf`: `SHA256:<base64>`. The `SHA256:` prefix is optional.

B.name: Authorization
B.description: Authorization configuration used when calling this endpoint. An `Sftp` endpoint requires `BasicUsername` and a `BasicPassword` and/or an `SshKey`.

B.name: Endpoint
B.description: The endpoint to send the events to. A valid HTTPS endpoint for `Http`, or `sftp://host[:port]` for `Sftp`.

B.name: HostKeys
B.description: The SSH host keys to pin on an `Sftp` endpoint. An `Sftp` endpoint can only be enabled when it has at least one. At most 20.

B.name: IgnoreNullValues
B.description: If false, the endpoint will also send `null` values. Preferred is true.

B.name: Name
B.description: A name to identify the configuration.

B.name: Status
B.description:
The status of the configuration.
Possible values:

* `1` - Enabled
* `2` - Disabled
* `3` - Error

B.name: TimeoutSeconds
B.description: Timeout after which requests are cancelled. Defaults to 5 seconds for an `Http` endpoint. For an `Sftp` endpoint it is not set by default and the timeout of the integration that uses the endpoint applies; a value above 0 replaces that timeout for every operation (for example the 15 minutes that the StepXml integration allows for reading and writing), up to a maximum of 3600 seconds. Not recommended to change.

B.name: Type
B.description:
The type of the endpoint configuration. Defaults to `Http`. It cannot be changed after creation.
Possible values:

* `1` - Http
* `2` - Sftp

B.name: UseStringIDs
B.description: If true, the endpoint will use string IDs instead of long IDs.

H.name: Code
H.description: A unique ID identifying this error.

H.name: Message
H.description: A human-readable message describing the error.

H.name: RequestID
H.description: A unique ID identifying the request. Please provide this ID when contacting support.

H.name: Type
H.description: A short description of the error type.

I.name: ExternalIDs
I.description: When using the `ExternalIDs` mode, this will hold the resolved external IDs.

I.name: IsAsyncResultAvailable
I.description: This is a flag indicating whether the async request is done. If it is `null`, it is not an async service. If it is `false`, the response is not yet available. Do not process the properties in that case. It is is `true` the properties are filled with the result of the call.

I.name: UnresolvedExternalIDs
I.description: When using the `ExternalIDs` mode, this will hold the external IDs we couldn't resolve.

G.name: ID
G.description: This is the ID of a `EndpointConfiguration`

G.name: SecretKey1
G.description: Make sure to store this information, this is the only time EVA will expose it for you!

G.name: SecretKey2
G.description: Make sure to store this information, this is the only time EVA will expose it for you!
